NEW DELHI: A plea has been filed in the Supreme Court against Chief Election Commissioner (CEC) Gyanesh Kumar over alleged unilateral decisions taken in connection with the Election Commission (ECI) electoral roll revision exercise, including the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of the electoral roll. The petitioner has also sought a Special Investigation Team (SIT) inquiry into the alleged deletion of around 13 crore voters from electoral rolls.The plea seeks a declaration that decisions allegedly taken without the concurrence of the other two election commissioners are illegal and calls for restoration of the original Form 6 used for voter registration. It also seeks prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar, deputy election commissioner Maneesh Garg and ECI IT head Seema Khanna for alleged violations of duties under the Representation of the People Act.The petition follows a report by The Indian Express stating that Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally objected at least 14 times over the past 10 months to decisions concerning the addition, deletion and restoration of voters and changes to the voter registration process.The petitioner has sought prosecution of Gyanesh Kumar under Section 32 of the Representation of the People Act.EC has maintained that all decisions, including those relating to SIR, were unanimous and taken with the approval of both Election Commissioners and the CEC.
Article Summary: The plea also seeks a sit inquiry into the alleged deletion of 13 crore voters from electoral rolls. Ec has maintained that all decisions, including those relating to sir, were unanimous and taken with the approval of both election commissioners and the cec.

Article Title: Veeramani Pocso case: Photo of TVK minister with Gem Granites chief surfaces; DMK says 'take action'

NEW DELHI: DMK spokesperson T K S Elangovan hit back at allegations linking the party to Gem Granites chairman R Veeramani, saying the DMK should not be blamed for the alleged actions of an individual. His remarks came as Chennai police constituted a four-member Special Investigation Team (SIT) to probe allegations of sexual offences against minor girls involving Veeramani.“They want to accuse the DMK for all those things. Today, there was a photograph on social media showing two ministers sitting with Veeramani. I don't understand anything,” Elangovan said.He added that Veeramani had been arrested and that the party leadership had also called for action if he was found to have committed any wrongdoing.“They have arrested him, and our leader also issued a statement that if he has committed a mistake, take action,” Elangovan said.Earlier, while talking to ANI, advocate and DMK leader NR Elango said "TN minister CTR Nirmal Kumar has falsely stated that the Veeramani case was diluted during the DMK regime. The case was registered on 07.12.2025 and investigated by the police. Houses were searched and further investigation was conducted based on the available evidence.The police had only stated that since adequate evidence was not yet available, complete investigation reports have not been filed so far, and that the further investigation is deferred until proper evidence is obtained—not that the case was dropped. The investigation was never dropped during the DMK regime."An SIT team has been formed as the investigation expands following the arrests of Veeramani and his associates.The SIT will be headed by Additional Commissioner of Police PC Thenmozhi of the Central Crime Branch. Joint Commissioner of Police N Disha Mittal, Superintendent of Police Mutharasi and Deputy Commissioner of Police Geethanjali of the Central Women and Children unit are the other members of the team.Veeramani was arrested along with Shanthi and Mahendra Simhan on August 29 in connection with the POCSO case. A former Gem Granites employee, Ganesan, was subsequently arrested on September 22 after police allegedly found a video linked to the case on his mobile phone.Veeramani was arrested after a USB drive containing a video clip that purportedly showed a juvenile girl being sexually assaulted by him in Oct 2025. Police said they identified the survivor and established that she was a minor when the alleged offence took place in 2019.
Article Summary: Dmk spokesperson t k s elangovan hit back at allegations linking the party to gem granites chairman r veeramani. He said the dmk should not be blamed for the alleged actions of an individual. His remarks came as chennai police constituted a four-member special investigation team (sit) to probe allegations.

NEW DELHI: US mercenary Aaron VanDyke, who was arrested by the National Investigation Agency (NIA) earlier this year in the Myanmar terror training case, was released from the Tihar jail after after a special NIA court granted permission to travel to the USA to meet their families for one month.The NIA court, along with Matthew Aaron Vandyke, gave permission to 6 Ukrainian nationals to travel to Ukraine subject to certain conditions and formalities.The court directed the release of their passports to them. Article Title: Tarun Tejpal challenges rape conviction, SC seeks Goa govt response
Article Text:
Tejpal surrendered before a Goa court on September 14

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has issued notice to the Goa government on a plea filed by former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal challenging the Bombay high court judgment convicting him in a 2013 sexual assault case and sentencing him to 10 years’ rigorous imprisonment.The bench sought the state’s response on Tejpal’s challenge to the August 6 High Court verdict, which overturned his acquittal by a trial court in May 2021. The high court had convicted him of sexually assaulting a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in Goa in November 2013 and also imposed a fine of more than Rs 10 lakh, to be paid to the survivor.Tejpal surrendered before a Goa court on September 14 after the Supreme Court directed him to do so within three weeks. He was subsequently sent to Central Jail at Colvale in North Goa to serve his sentence.
Article Summary: The supreme court has issued notice to the goa government on a plea filed by former tehelka editor-in-chief tarun tejpal. He was convicted of sexually assaulting a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in goa in november 2013. The high court had also imposed a fine of more than rs 10 lakh, to be paid to the survivor.

NEW DELHI: A fresh landslide in Rimbi village under the Yuksom-Tashiding constituency of West Sikkim triggered a mudslide on Friday, sending large amounts of mud, rocks and debris downhill amid continued rainfall.The landslide has raised concerns among residents as nearby houses, properties and road connectivity remain at risk. No loss of life has been reported so far in the incident, news agency ANI reported.The Rimbi incident was among several landslide-related disruptions reported in Sikkim following heavy overnight rainfall.A landslide also struck Tadong in Sikkim's Gangtok late on Thursday night following heavy rainfall. A video of the incident showed rocks, mud and debris crashing down the hillside.Last week, another landslide in Lingding, Tadong, damaged part of a house, with mud and rainwater entering rooms on the first floor. Three water pipelines were also damaged, affecting the local water supply.The road near Lingding Jhora remained inaccessible for several hours, from around 3am to 9am, before debris was cleared and traffic movement was restored.No injuries or deaths were reported in the incident.In another development, 128 people from 28 houses in vulnerable areas of Rimbi in Gyalshing district were shifted to safer locations following fresh landslide activity and heavy rainfall, according to the Sikkim state disaster management authority.Relief and restoration operations were carried out in Rimbi and Singlitam, with the administration providing assistance to affected residents and clearing accumulated debris.Authorities have urged residents to stay away from active landslide zones and exercise caution as rainfall continues.

NEW DELHI: Congress on Friday upped the ante against Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and put up posters demanding his removal in Delhi amid the ongoing row over the functioning of the poll panel and Special Intensive Revision of electoral list.Put up by the Delhi Pradesh Congress Committee's OBC department, the poster read, "Remove Gyanesh Kumar, save Election Commission."This came a day after Leader of Opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi lashed out at Gyanesh Kumar after reports of differences within the poll body over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls sparked a political stir.Rahul accused the CEC of "vote chori, kanun chori, sanstha chori (vote theft, law theft, institutional theft)", calling it an "act against the nation"."The Election Commission is the institutional protector of the vote... I have shown it with proof, and there is already more than enough information to make this a 100% certainty that Indian elections, Lok Sabha elections, 2024 election, Vidhan Sabha elections are all being rigged," he said, addressing a press conference."I come from a political family, and I have spent more than 50 years in a political family... In India, there is a fundamental force called anti-incumbency that very quickly starts to resist any government.It does not spare anybody. Indira Gandhi won the Bangladesh war, was at the height of her popularity, and then suddenly, within a year or two, massive anti-incumbency, massive pressure," he added.Meanwhile, police personnel have been deployed outside the Election Commission office in Delhi ahead of a protest demonstration by Delhi Congress over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls and demands for the resignation of Gyanesh Kumar.The Indian Youth Congress is also scheduled to hold a protest march from 5, Raisina Road to Jantar Mantar on Friday, demanding the resignation of Kumar.The Indian Youth Congress (IYC) on Thursday also launched a nationwide online citizens' petition titled "Gyanesh, It's Done Bro", seeking action against the CEC and calling upon citizens, particularly young people, to participate in a campaign for electoral transparency and accountability.An Indian Express report has highlighted differences among members of the EC over the SIR of electoral rolls. The report said Election Commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi raised formal objections on at least 14 occasions over a 10-month period against decisions and orders related to electoral-roll processes.The Election Commission, however, described the queries and observations raised by its members as part of its routine internal process. It said written notes, technical inputs and internal scrutiny were standard mechanisms to check legal compliance and protect voters' rights.The ECI further said all decisions taken by the Commission, including those related to SIR, had full legal backing and stressed that its final decisions were unanimous.

Article Title: 'Dubai-based scammers looted Rs 94,000 crore': CBI arrests Mahadev app key accused deported from UAE

CBI on Thursday arrested Abhishek Kumar, a key accused in the Mahadev online betting and gambling case in which Enforcement Directorate (ED) has claimed that the perpetrators of the illegal activities have so far generated and laundered proceeds of crime of more than Rs 94,000 crore.Kumar was deported from the UAE and taken into custody by CBI immediately after he arrived at Hyderabad airport from Dubai. He was close to main accused Saurabh Chandrakar and Shubham Soni - both continue to operate the gambling network from the UAE and other jurisdictions.Kumar coordinated various panels in the Mahadev network and was responsible for collecting funds and acquiring immovable assets in Dubai out of ill-gotten proceeds of crime, a CBI spokesperson said. He has been taken to Raipur and produced before a special court for police remand. So far, seven Red Corner Notices and two extradition requests have been pending against other accused.The Mahadev online betting and gambling app is still active and proceeds of crime of Rs 94,000 crore have been generated so far by the accused, who are in Dubai, ED has said in its latest chargesheet in the case. More than Rs 1,000 crore has been invested in Indian share markets through foreign portfolio investments (FPIs), the agency said.It estimated that in the last few years, the accused generated more than Rs 11,000 crore annually from illegal online gambling and betting activities.Based on analysis of various seized digital evidence and statements of several accused, ED said that "it can be estimated that proceeds of crime worth Rs 11,400 crore (approx) must have been generated by illegal operations of Mahadev online book every year". The gambling network has been running since 2019."As per latest findings, Mahadev app is still running a huge number of panels. Estimated proceeds of crime generated by the app is around Rs 75,000-80,000 crore during the last seven years," ED has said. In addition, it said other illegal apps run by the syndicate like Skyexchange.com and Lotus365.com have generated proceeds of crime of over Rs 14,000 crore."A majority of the proceeds of crime was layered and transferred to the promoters based in Dubai," ED stated.The agency has so far attached assets worth over Rs 2,000 crore linked to various accused. The agency said the above estimation of proceeds of crime is only a provisional figure and is likely to go up.
Article Summary: Abhishek kumar was deported from the uae and taken into custody by cbi. Article Title: Wangchuk fears 'encounter' after accusing govt of Ladakh atrocities

: Climate activist Sonam Wangchuk said Thursday he feared he could be subjected to an “encounter” for speaking out against what he called atrocities in Ladakh, a year after police firing killed four protesters in Leh.Drawing a comparison with Tibet, Wangchuk said Ladakhis had chosen India because of its democracy. “Today, such atrocities are being committed in Ladakh that even China is not doing in Tibet. That is what you are seeing today,” he said, addressing a gathering on the first anniversary of the police firing on Sept 24, 2025.He sought a people’s tribunal to probe the killings, saying a judicial commission set up by Union home ministry had yet to submit its report.“Last year on this day, four people died... Bullets hit their chests, backs, and heads. Those were not pellets that would merely injure you or hurt your eyes. Bullets were fired indiscriminately from automatic weapons, like AK-47s, at the unarmed youth of Ladakh who were peacefully demanding their rights,” Wangchuk alleged.He rejected claims that the protests were triggered by him. He alleged that before the 2020 LAHDC-Leh elections, Ladakhi representatives opposed to holding polls were taken to New Delhi on a special flight and promised statehood and Sixth Schedule status.He blamed “govt failure to honour those promises” for last year’s demonstrations.Authorities imposed curfew-like restrictions in Leh after the alleged “arson and rioting” and subsequent police firing. FIRs were filed and 81 people arrested, including Wangchuk. He was charged under NSA and sent to Jodhpur jail. After 170 days, Union govt withdrew his detention on March 14 this year and he was set free.He feared further action, saying: “They sent me to jail. Inquiries have been made against me. Only an encounter is left. I am ready for that. It is my last wish. Experts tell me that you will be subjected to an encounter. So be it. Let the country wake up, this is my hope.”A complete shutdown was observed in Leh on Thursday, designated as Martyr’s Day. Wangchuk accused authorities of stopping people from attending the rally, a claim denied by police.Police said Ladakh Buddhist Association had sought permission for a public meeting at Leh’s NDS stadium, which has a capacity of 10,000. The administration granted permission for a prayer meet from 10am to noon. Police reported a turnout of 800 at the event and denied allegations that they erected barricades to stop people from reaching the venue.

Article Title: Centre pleads for prospective effect of SC creamy layer ruling
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Facing the task of implementing Supreme Court's ruling on calculating creamy layer criteria for OBC reservation from the retrospective date of 2012, Centre pleaded with the court to make the enforcement of the verdict prospective and grant it two years' time to implement it.The court had in March held that the income of parents could not be the sole criterion to determine the creamy layer of a candidate for exclusion from OBC reservation, and status and category of a parent's job had to be considered with an 'income/wealth test' as an additional criterion. It made the verdict implementable from 2012, when the case was first filed.In a written note filed by additional solicitor general Aishwarya Bhati, govt submitted that the retrospective application of a changed eligibility criterion may unsettle appointments and admissions made under the rules and certificates prevailing at the time and create uncertainty regarding OBC-NCL status, seniority, service conditions and career progression."The retrospective implementation of the present judgement would create changes in candidates' service and cadre allocation... as it would affect the services of persons appointed on the basis of CSE-2012 onward and cause a cascading effect among civil servants... The aforementioned cascading effect will impact not only OBC candidates but also reverberate across all categories including (unreserved category) of the civil services," the note said.Govt said a reasonable time of two years should be given to it to undertake the necessary exercise of establishing equivalence of posts, after consulting all the stakeholders and formulating a uniform policy/mechanism for determination of OBC creamy layer status."Union of India is only praying for a limited deferral of the operationalisation of the law laid down by this hon'ble court for a period of two years so that the competing rights can be adjusted consistent with the administrative contingencies and an effective equivalence exercise is carried out," it said.
Article Summary: Supreme court's ruling on calculating creamy layer criteria for obc reservation from retrospective date of 2012. Centre pleaded with the court to make the enforcement of the verdict prospective and grant it two years' time to implement it.

NEW DELHI: PM Narendra Modi is learnt to have told ministers that knowing facts and communicating them effectively was crucial as he asked them to study issues in detail and put across govt’s position to counter negative narratives.The suggestion came during the two-day Chintan Shivir at a time when issues around Election Commission’s SIR exercise and the IIT-Bombay controversy have become political flashpoints. There were detailed presentations under themes, including “Self development along with improvement in functioning of their departments” and “Jan Vishwas se Jan Aadhaar” (trust-based governance to popular support).The session held after a gap of four years is being seen as a mid-term stocktaking exercise to review performance and chalk out strategies for improving overall efficiency of ministers and ministries. Urging ministers to engage with officials at all levels, PM Modi reportedly said it had come to his notice that a minister did not interact with officials below the secretary in the department while suggesting that interaction with officials of levels was necessary for better performance.PM, in his brief address, has asked ministers to ensure saturation of around 40-45 major welfare schemes and communicating their benefits effectively to the intended beneficiaries.

Article Title: NALSAR students screen Umar Khalid documentary after screenings cancelled at IIIT-Hyderabad, NLSIU
Article Text:
The screening was a private event restricted to students.

Prisoner No. 626710 is Present

Prisoner No. 626710 is Present





Hyderabad: The screening of Umar Khalid’s documentary,, which was cancelled at the International Institute of Information Technology, Hyderabad (IIIT-H), and National Law School of India University (NLSIU), Bengaluru, was held at NALSAR University of Law in the city on Wednesday evening. A group of students who independently organised the “solidarity screening” said it was held to offer an opportunity “to engage directly with the film’s questions about rights, accountability and the human cost of prolonged incarceration, while expressing solidarity with those affected by these failures of the justice system”.The screening was a private event restricted to students.“The film raises urgent concerns about the delay in the justice system, and about undertrial prisoners being kept in custody for years without their trials even beginning,” one of the students told TOI via email. “When a person remains imprisoned for six years without trial, the delay itself becomes a serious denial of justice. Law cannot, and should not, be used as a tool of violence without convictions. The process cannot become the punishment,” the email added.NALSAR students have called on student bodies across universities to organise similar screenings of the documentary.The documentary has not been certified by the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC).The board has stated that screening an uncertified film would violate the Cinematograph Act unless a specific exemption has been obtained.Last week, the screening at IIIT-H was cancelled after the CBFC flagged the issue on X. The institute later said that the proposed event had not been organised or authorised by its management. At NLSIU, too, the event, which was initially postponed, was later cancelled after organisers said they faced threats of criminal action, intimidation, doxxing and other forms of harassment., directed by filmmaker Lalit Vachani, is a documentary about Khalid, tracing his journey from student activist to his arrest in 2020 and subsequent incarceration.Meanwhile, NALSAR vice-chancellor, Prof Srikrishna Deva Rao, said, “NALSAR University of Law did not authorise screening of the documentary film Prisoner No 626710 on its campus. No official permission for the same was given to anybody by any University authority,”
Article Summary: The screening was a private event restricted to students. Nalsar students have called on student bodies across universities to organise similar screenings of the documentary. The documentary has not been certified by the central board of film certification (cbfc) the board has stated that screening an uncertified film would violate the cinematograph act unless a specific exemption has been obtained.

Article Title: ‘Jaldi kar, Panvel nikalna hai’: How Rajat Sood's comedy show turned ugly at Ahmedabad’s Nirma University
Article Text:

What happened during the event

AHMEDABAD: "Jaldi kar, Panvel nikalna hai," an alleged remark by a student during a comedy show at Nirma University in Ahmedabad has sparked controversy after a video purportedly showing a professor grabbing the student's collar went viral on social media.The incident allegedly took place during 'Technofora 2026', a three-day event organised by students of the university's Institute of Technology from September 18 to 20.According to the claims surrounding the video, a professor and head of the electrical and instrumentation department was addressing students when the student shouted the remark, referring to a dialogue from the Bollywood film 'Golmaal'.The professor then called the student on stage and allegedly grabbed him by the collar, as seen in the video.The professor is also heard threatening the student, saying, "I can go to any extent. The day you dare to insult any faculty member of the Nirma University campus, you are gone forever."The incident occured during a stand-up comedy show featuring comedian Rajat Sood.The Congress-affiliated National Students' Union of India (NSUI) has demanded an apology from the professor and an inquiry into the incident.NSUI state vice president Vedant Tomar said, “The professor must apologise to the student and the university should conduct an impartial inquiry into the incident.”Bhavik Solanki, national coordinator of the NSUI, claimed in a statement that the student was subjected to inappropriate behaviour and also demanded an apology from the professor and an inquiry.The NSUI said it would hold a protest if its demands were not met.The private university did not respond to an email seeking its comment on the incident.The circumstances leading to the confrontation, including the student's alleged remark and the professor's response, could not be independently verified.
Article Summary: A video purportedly showing a professor grabbing the student's collar went viral on social media. The incident allegedly took place during 'technofora 2026', a three-day event organised by students of the university's institute of technology. The congress-affiliated national students' union of india has demanded an apology from the professor and an inquiry into the incident.

Article Title: 'All elections rigged, laws illegal': Rahul Gandhi attacks Centre over EC-SIR row; BJP calls it 'jooth ki goonj'

NEW DELHI: Congress leader and leader of opposition in the Lok Sabha Rahul Gandhi on Thursday escalated his attack on the Centre and the Election Commission over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging that India's elections had been "rigged" and demanding the immediate resignation of chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar.Congress MP said Prime Minister Narendra Modi, Union home minister Amit Shah and Kumar were "deshdrohis" (traitors) for what he alleged was the destruction of the country's vote.He said the 2024 Lok Sabha and assembly elections were "all rigged" and asserted that PM Modi and Shah would be investigated over what he described as a conspiracy to "steal elections".His remarks came a day after an investigation by a media report claimed that election commissioners Sukhbir Singh Sandhu and Vivek Joshi had formally raised objections to decisions and orders related to electoral-roll management and the SIR exercise.The Election Commission has rejected the suggestion that these objections reflected a disagreement over its final decisions, saying its decisions, including those concerning SIR, were unanimous.Addressing a press conference at the Congress headquarters in New Delhi, Rahul said the Election Commission was responsible for protecting the vote and accused the poll panel of failing in that duty."Mr Gyanesh Kumar must resign immediately. We are not going to let democracy be destroyed in India and sit silent, and the people responsible for this are going to be punished," Rae Bareli MP said.He said the reported objections by Sandhu and Joshi showed that questions were being raised within the poll panel itself."The two Election Commissioners have done a wise thing, and I appreciate it," he said.Former Congress president further alleged that the Prime Minister and home minister were "at the top of this conspiracy" and would be investigated. He also suggested that Kumar should "turn approver", describing that as an act of nationalism."I can say with certainty that Indian elections -- 2024 Lok Sabha and Vidhan Sabha polls -- were all rigged," Rahul said.He also linked the alleged manipulation of votes to the functioning of Parliament, laws and institutions."From vote chori (vote theft), comes kanoon chori (law theft) and from that comes sanstha chori (institutional theft)," he said.Explaining the argument, the Congress leader said the vote was the foundation of the constitutional system."If the vote has been destroyed, then our Constitution has been destroyed. If our Constitution has been destroyed, our laws are illegal. If our laws are illegal, our institutions are meaningless," he said.He said the alleged issue was therefore not limited to electoral rolls but concerned the wider constitutional framework."The central question here is this is not just an attack on the vote; this is an attack on the idea, the basic infrastructure, and the expression of every single Indian person," Rahul said.The immediate trigger was an Indian Express investigation reporting that Sandhu and Joshi recorded at least 14 objections over 10 months to decisions and orders issued in the name of the Election Commission.The objections reportedly covered voter registration and deletion, changes to Form 6 used for new voter registration, access to and centralisation of electoral-roll databases, and other aspects of the SIR exercise.The report said the two commissioners had objected four times on a single day and had raised concerns about decisions they said were taken without their knowledge or approval.The Election Commission, however, has disputed the interpretation that the reported internal notes amounted to a breakdown or disagreement over final decisions.The poll panel said internal technical notes, queries and suggestions were part of the normal administrative and decision-making process and maintained that the final decisions of the Commission were unanimous. Its response did not dispute the existence of the notes but said focusing on individual objections presented only part of the overall decision-making process.The EC's position is that all decisions relating to SIR had the approval of CEC Gyanesh Kumar and election commissioners Sandhu and Joshi.The BJP hit back at Lok Sabha LoP's allegations, with party spokesperson Pradeep Bhandari describing his press conference as a "damp squib" and dubbing it "Jhoot Ki Goonj".In a post on X, Bhandari accused Rahul of making false claims and said the Congress leader was unable to win public support through democratic means.He also challenged Rahul's assertion that there had been no anti-incumbency against the BJP since 2014, saying the BJP had lost 20 elections since then.BJP leader and MP Sudhanshu Trivedi also challenged Rae Bareli MP's argument on anti-incumbency.He pointed to the Congress's electoral record in states including Tamil Nadu and West Bengal and argued that anti-incumbency had affected the Congress as well.On the media report, Trivedi questioned the basis for treating the reported objections as evidence that the Election Commission's final decisions were not unanimous."Do you have even a single report indicating that a decision was not unanimous?" Trivedi said, adding that there was no quoted statement from any Election Commissioner saying that a final decision had not been unanimous.He also questioned whether the reported internal objections should be treated as evidence of a wider institutional dispute when the Commission had maintained that its decisions were unanimous.A significant part of the Congress leader's press conference focused on what he described as the disappearance of anti-incumbency against the BJP.He cited electoral swings in Haryana, Maharashtra, Uttar Pradesh, Madhya Pradesh and Gujarat, and said governments and political parties in India had historically faced anti-incumbency."Haryana swings from one party to another for 50 years. Suddenly anti-incumbency disappears. Maharashtra swings; suddenly it disappears. Uttar Pradesh swings. Sometimes Samajwadi, sometimes BSP; it disappears. Madhya Pradesh, it disappears. Gujarat, it disappears," Rahul said.He cited former prime minister Indira Gandhi's experience after the 1971 Bangladesh war as an example of how anti-incumbency, according to him, had affected even highly popular leaders."It happens to leader after leader. It does not happen to PM Modi, Shah and the BJP - now we know the answer to it," he said.He also played videos of PM Modi and Shah, including remarks about the BJP remaining in power for decades and Modi's "Abki Baar 400 Paar" slogan. He argued that such statements were inconsistent with the normal operation of democratic politics.However, BJP has rejected Rahul's allegations, while the Election Commission has maintained that the reported objections were part of its internal decision-making process and that its final decisions, including those related to SIR, were unanimous.The dispute over the electoral-roll revision and the reported objections by the two election commissioners is now at the centre of the political exchange between Congress, BJP and the poll panel.
Article Summary: Congress leader and leader of opposition in the lok sabha rahul gandhi escalated his attack on the centre and the election commission. He alleged that india's elections had been "rigged" and demanded the immediate resignation of chief election commissioner gyanesh kumar.

Article Title: 'No eligible elector will be left behind': Goa CEO clarifies on 97 missing voters

NEW DELHI: The Office of the Chief Electoral Officer of Goa on Thursday clarified the controversy surrounding 97 voters who were not included in the final electoral roll published in February 2026, saying the cases were subsequently processed through house-to-house visits and that many of the voters have since been enrolled.In a press note shared on X, the CEO's office said the 97 cases were separately processed by Booth Level Officers (BLOs) for completion of Form 6, the application used for inclusion of names in the electoral roll."Many have since been enrolled, while the remaining cases are being processed," the office said, adding that no eligible elector would be left out.The clarification comes amid a controversy over the exclusion of the 97 voters following Goa's Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.According to an Indian Express report, the 97 voters had initially been flagged during the SIR process for what the Election Commission described as "logical discrepancies" in the electoral database.These discrepancies could arise from issues such as mismatches while linking an elector to parents or grandparents in older electoral rolls.The affected voters were subsequently given an opportunity to submit documents and objections.In Goa, 649 electors came forward, following which Electoral Registration Officers (EROs) and Assistant EROs examined their cases. Officials found 97 cases where the earlier decisions needed to be reversed and the voters were eligible for inclusion.However, the final electoral roll published on February 21, 2026, did not include the 97 names.The issue subsequently drew attention to the Election Commission's ECINet electoral-roll software.According to an Indian Express investigation, the Goa CEO's office sent eight communications between February 11 and 17 seeking a rollback or reversion facility that would allow the earlier deletion decisions to be reversed.The controversy has also triggered criticism from opposition parties, which have questioned the functioning and centralisation of the electoral-roll system.
Article Summary: The office of the chief electoral officer of goa on thursday clarified the controversy surrounding 97 voters who were not included in the final electoral roll published in february 2026. The office said the cases were subsequently processed through house-to-house visits and that many of the voters have since been enrolled.

Article Title: SC flags ‘false’ POCSO cases in marital disputes, bars immediate arrest of accused parent
Article Text:
Rape-murder of A law student: Petitioner Ameer-Ul-Islam seeking transfer from Viyyur Central Prison in Kerala to a jail in Assam

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday laid down safeguards against the immediate arrest of a parent or family member accused under the POCSO Act when the alleged offence involves a child living under the same roof and there is a matrimonial dispute between the child's parents.A bench of Justices J B Pardiwala and K V Viswanathan, flagging a rise in fakecases, said police should not act in haste in such cases and directed that, as a general rule, an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology should evaluate the child before authorities decide whether there is sufficient reason to arrest the accused.The court said the safeguards were necessary in cases where allegations may be influenced by a strained relationship between the parents. It stressed that the measures do not dilute the seriousness of offences under the Protection of Children from Sexual Offences (POCSO) Act, but are intended to ensure that the power of arrest is exercised after considering all relevant circumstances.The court said immediate arrest should not take place when two conditions are present: a POCSO offence is alleged against a parent or family member living with the child, and a matrimonial dispute exists between the child's parents, whether or not the dispute is pending before a court.The police officer receiving the complaint must verify whether such a matrimonial dispute exists, the court said. "When the above-stated threshold conditions are met, post the registration of an FIR, we are of the considered opinion that the investigating officer should not act in haste or take coercive actions in the form of arrest immediately," the bench added, as quoted by PTI.The verdict came in a matrimonial dispute involving an estranged Bengaluru couple. The wife had alleged that the child was sexually assaulted. The case was investigated by the CBI, which found the allegation to be false. The Supreme Court restored custody of the child to the father, taking into account the welfare of the minor.The court also directed the investigating officer or the Special Juvenile Police Unit to seek the services of an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology, in consultation with the District Child Protection Unit or, where one is unavailable, the District Legal Services Authority, adding that the expert's evaluation must be conducted independently and without influence from either the parent or investigating authorities.After receiving the evaluation, investigators must consider the expert's opinion along with other evidence and circumstances before deciding whether there is "reason to believe" that the accused committed the offence and whether an arrest is warranted. The court said an exception could be made in cases where the material available is "palpable", allowing the investigating officer to dispense with an expert evaluation, but reasons for doing so must be recorded in writing.The bench also stressed that arrest is not automatically required merely because an offence is cognisable. The court said an arrest can cause "irreparable harm" to an accused parent or family member, particularly where the allegation later turns out to be unfounded.The Supreme Court also raised concerns about the consequences of allegations on children and their relationship with the accused parent."The trauma that a child is put through in the process and the accusation can damage the very fabric of the parent-child relationship," the bench said, adding that such a wound could leave an "indelible scar" on both the child and parent.The court also flagged what it described as an increase in false allegations in matrimonial disputes."What is alarming is that this tendency of making false accusations is on the rise," it said.The bench cautioned against parents being influenced by advisers during matrimonial disputes, saying that some may be driven by a "win at any cost" approach.At the same time, the court said the safeguards were not a finding that allegations made in such circumstances are false. Investigating authorities must examine the allegations along with the surrounding circumstances and other evidence.For complaints filed directly before a special court, the Supreme Court said an order taking cognisance and summoning an accused must demonstrate application of mind. The special court should also involve an expert in child and adolescent psychiatry or clinical psychology to evaluate the child and submit a report.
Article Summary: Supreme court lays down safeguards against the immediate arrest of a parent or family member accused under the pocso act. Justices j b pardiwala and k v viswanathan said police should not act in haste in such cases. The court said the safeguards were necessary in cases where allegations may be influenced by a strained relationship between the parents.

Article Title: 'No trust in EC': Akhilesh Yadav alleges ‘vote theft’ in 2022 UP polls, says SP will contest 2027 in alliance
Article Text:
Akhilesh Yadav greets the crowd at the party's PDA Rath Yatra campaign for the 2027 Assembly elections, in Raebareli

Akhilesh links 2022 result to alleged 'vote theft'

SP says 2027 alliance will depend on winnability

Yadav attacks BJP over UCC, jobs and schools

NEW DELHI: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav on Thursday accused the Election Commission of facilitating what he called "vote theft" of the PDA bloc in the 2022 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections, claiming that his party would have formed the government had the alleged irregularities not taken place.Addressing a public meeting in Raebareli after arriving on the party's specially designed PDA Rath, Yadav also said the SP would contest the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections in alliance, with seat-sharing based on the ability of a candidate or party to win."The Election Commission has been exposed and has worked like a puppet. Such a low level of work may never have happened in a democracy. Now, there is no trust in the Election Commission," Yadav said.The PDA acronym, coined by Yadav in 2023, refers to Pichhde (backward classes), Dalits and Alpsankhyak (minorities).Yadav alleged that the BJP was using the election machinery because it knew people would not vote for the party on issues such as inflation.He claimed that the alleged "vote theft" in the 2022 Assembly polls had prevented the SP from forming the government in Uttar Pradesh.The SP chief also attacked what he described as "bulldozer politics", saying the PDA movement would challenge it in the 2027 elections."This time (in 2027) the electoral verdict would not merely defeat them but would 'demolish' and permanently eliminate such negative politics," he said.Yadav also referred to the 2024 Lok Sabha election, saying, "We defeated them in 2024 and in 2027 we will work for their (BJP) permanent defeat."The SP and Congress had contested the 2024 Lok Sabha election in Uttar Pradesh as allies, winning 37 and six seats respectively, for a combined tally of 43. The BJP won 33 seats in the state.Yadav said the SP would contest the 2027 polls as part of an alliance, although he did not specify its partners or the number of seats each party would contest."We will have an alliance," he said, adding that the basis for deciding seats would be winnability."Whoever can win a seat should get that seat," Yadav asserted.His remarks come as the SP and Congress face the question of whether they can maintain their alliance for the next Uttar Pradesh Assembly election.Yadav's PDA Rath campaign was launched from Raebareli, where Congress leader Rahul Gandhi is the sitting Lok Sabha MP. The SP had said Yadav's visit also included a planned meeting with Harchandpur MLA Rahul Lodhi, following a September 17 clash involving members of the Samajwadi Chhatra Sabha and ABVP.Police had denied allegations of manhandling by SP workers and said a magisterial inquiry into the police action had been ordered.The specially designed PDA Rath carries slogans including "Samajwadi PDA Yatra" and "PDA hi parivartan layega", along with the definition of PDA as Pichhda, Dalit, Alpsankhyak.Yadav also criticised the BJP over the alleged demolition of religious structures in Kashi and Saharanpur, accusing the party of pursuing communal politics and weakening social harmony.On the proposed Uniform Civil Code , he said laws should follow efforts to ensure equality among citizens."We say first make the citizens equal; first, let all of us become one. When everyone's respect becomes equal, then bring laws to increase that respect and take people forward," he said.On employment, Yadav promised that an SP government would increase government recruitment and provide jobs to young people."If outsourcing has to be ended, we will end outsourcing," he said.He also promised free treatment in hospitals, saying people would not have to search for a card before receiving healthcare.Yadav accused the state government of shutting primary schools while opening liquor shops and said an SP government would reopen schools that had been closed.He also promised to restore the old pension scheme for government employees.The Raebareli visit marks the beginning of the SP's PDA-focused outreach ahead of the 2027 Assembly election, with Yadav using the campaign to reiterate his allegations against the Election Commission, outline his alliance strategy and present the party's key electoral promises.
Article Summary: Akhilesh yadav accuses the election commission of facilitating what he called "vote theft" of the pda bloc in the 2022 uttar pradesh assembly elections. Yadav claims his party would have formed the government had the alleged irregularities not taken place.

Article Title: 'No anti-incumbency against BJP?' Party counters Rahul Gandhi with Tamil Nadu, Bengal poll history
Article Text:
BJP counters Rahul Gandhi with Tamil Nadu, Bengal poll history

What Rahul Gandhi said

NEW DELHI: Congress leader Rahul Gandhi 's claim that anti-incumbency has “disappeared” for the BJP because of its alleged collusion with the Election Commission drew a sharp response from the ruling party. BJP national spokesperson Sudhanshu Trivedi cited the Congress's electoral record in states including Tamil Nadu, West Bengal, Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Odisha to hit back at leader of opposition in Lok Sabha.Rahul Gandhi, speaking at a press conference in New Delhi on Thursday amid the ongoing row over the Election Commission and the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, questioned how anti-incumbency could seemingly affect successive governments but not the BJP.Responding to Rahul's remarks, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi questioned his understanding of Indian electoral history and argued that the stronger long-term anti-incumbency trend was against the Congress."From a political point of view, his wisdom is zero, his knowledge is zero," Trivedi said, launching a personal attack on Rahul.Trivedi then pointed to states where the Congress has not returned to power for decades."Yes, anti-incumbency is indeed very strong and consistent against Congress," he said.On Tamil Nadu, Trivedi said the Congress had not returned to power since 1967, arguing that the BJP was not even a significant political force in the state at the time. In West Bengal, he said, the Congress had not returned to government since 1977.The Election Commission's statistical reports list assembly elections across the states and provide the historical electoral data on which such comparisons can be made.The BJP spokesperson also cited Bihar, Uttar Pradesh and Odisha, saying there had been no Congress government in Bihar after 1990, no Congress government in Uttar Pradesh after 1989 and no Congress government in Odisha since 1999."Ever since transparent elections have taken place, CCTV cameras have come in, and independent media has arrived, they've started finding it difficult to come to power," Trivedi said.Earlier in the day, Rahul held a press conference in which he cited former PM Indira Gandhi as an example, saying she was at the height of her popularity after the 1971 Bangladesh war but faced "massive anti-incumbency" within a year or two."The same thing happens to leader after leader, to Congress leaders and to regional parties. But, for some reason, it does not happen to PM Modi, Amit Shah and the BJP," Rahul Gandhi said.He also pointed to electoral changes in Haryana, Maharashtra and Uttar Pradesh, arguing that these states had historically seen voters shift between parties."Haryana swings from one party to another for 50 years, but suddenly anti-incumbency disappears. Maharashtra swings; suddenly that disappears. Uttar Pradesh swings, from the Samajwadi Party to the Bahujan Samaj Party, that also disappears," he said.Rahul said the question had been a "fundamental" one for the Congress until the party arrived at what he described as the answer: "vote chori".His remarks came as he stepped up his attack on the Election Commission over the SIR exercise. He accused chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar of undermining the electoral process, demanded his resignation and alleged that the destruction of votes would ultimately undermine the Constitution and institutions."From vote chori comes kanoon chori, and from that comes sanstha chori," he said.
Article Summary: Bjp counters rahul gandhi with tamil nadu, bengal poll history. Rahul gandhi says anti-incumbency has "disappeared" for the bjp because of its alleged collusion with the election commission. Bjp national spokesperson sudhanshu trivedi cited the congress's electoral record in states including tamil nadu and west bengal.

Article Title: 'Jhoot ki goonj by frustrated leader': BJP mocks Rahul Gandhi's presser on EC-SIR row

BJP mocks Rahul Gandhi's presser on EC-SIR row

NEW DELHI: The BJP on Thursday mocked Congress leader Rahul Gandhi's presser in New Delhi, calling it a “damp squib” and accusing the leader of opposition in Lok Sabha of making false claims.BJP leader Pradeep Bhandari took a swipe at Rahul by twisting the name of his “Chhatron Ki Goonj” initiative, calling the Congress press conference “Jhoot Ki Goonj”.Taking to X, Bhandari wrote: "Rahul Gandhi's Press was a damp squib! It was "Jhoot Ki Goonj" by a frustrated leader not able to win People's support through democratic means."Bhandari then listed what he called two “lies” from Rahul's press conference and offered his counterpoints as "truths".The first, according to Bhandari, was Rahul's claim that there had been no anti-incumbency against the BJP since 2014. Countering it, Bhandari said: “BJP has lost 20 elections since 2014.”His second point was Rahul's question over how Prime Minister Narendra Modi had managed to win elections consecutively.Bhandari responded: “Did Congress under Nehru did "Vote Chori", or does Congress win in Rae Bareilly 16 times in consectutive.”BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi also countered Rahul's claims in his presser.Making a counter to Rahul's "no anti-incumbency for PM Modi" claim, BJP MP Sudhanshu Trivedi said, "He (Rahul Gandhi) stated that anti-incumbency is an established truth in this country and that this phenomenon has persisted since the BJP came to power. I feel that, politically speaking, Rahul Gandhi is devoid of wisdom and knowledge; he fails to grasp the reality. Anti-incumbency has certainly been very consistent and strong against the Congress. He lacks an understanding of Indian politics.""The Congress has never returned to power in Tamil Nadu since 1967, a time when the Bharatiya Janata Party did not even exist. The Congress has not returned to power in Bengal since 1977; the Communists ruled there for 34 years from 1977 to 2011, yet Rahul Gandhi neither understands nor sees this...And yet, he brings up the issue of anti-incumbency," Rajya Sabha member added.The BJP's counterattack came shortly after Rahul launched a fresh broadside at the Centre and the Election Commission over the special intensive revision (SIR), claiming that “all elections are being rigged”.Meanwhile, Rahul made a sweeping claim that “all elections are being rigged.”Former Congress president also said, “anti-incumbency does not happen to PM Modi.”“Gyanesh Kumar was chosen by PM, Amit Shah and now two ECs are saying he's responsible for chaos, damage to our voting system,” Rahul said.His latest attack came amid the row over the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) after an Indian Express report claimed there were differences between chief election commissioner Gyanesh Kumar and the other two election commissioners over the exercise.
Article Summary: Bjp leader pradeep bhandari took a swipe at rahul by twisting the name of his “chhatron ki goonj’ initiative. The bjp's counterattack came shortly after rahul launched a fresh broadside at the centre and the election commission over the special intensive revision.

Article Title: 6 Ukrainians accused of training armed rebels in India, Myanmar get default bail
Article Text:
Picture credit: Matthew Aaron VanDyke’s Social Media handles and official website (file photo)

NEW DELHI: An NIA court in Delhi Wednesday granted bail to six Ukrainian nationals arrested in March this year for allegedly running a training camp for ethnic armed rebels in India and Myanmar.The court, which ordered their release on a cash bond of Rs 1 lakh each, also discharged them from offences under the Immigration and Foreigners Act following after the Foreigners Regional Registration Office (FRRO), which deals with the immigration matters involving foreign nationals, settled the offences on payment of a penalty of Rs 5.5 lakh each.The offences, which pertained to illegal entry and visa violations, are compoundable at the level of the FRRO.Special judge Prashant Sharma granted them default bail on grounds of parity with their American co-accused Matthew Aaron Van Dyke.While granting bail to Dyke on Sept 18, the judge had dismissed the NIA’s opposition, observing that even if the probe was far from over, “at this stage it cannot be concluded that applicant/ accused Matthew Aaron Vandyke is not entitled for default bail”.Default bail is provisioned in the UAPA if the probe agency doesn’t file charge sheet containing offences under the anti-terror law with 180 days of arresting the accused. Following this, the court had directed that the other six accused could also seek default bail.Earlier this month, the agency filed a charge sheet which did not mention provisions of the UAPA, 1967, which was invoked in the initial FIR.
Article Summary: Six ukrainian nationals arrested in march this year for allegedly running a training camp for ethnic armed rebels in india and myanmar. The court discharged them from offences under the immigration and foreigners act following after the foreigners regional registration office settled the offences on payment of a penalty of rs 5.5 lakh each.

Article Title: Tamil Nadu Pocso case: Businessman Veeramani, aide arrested; what we know so far
Article Text:
Child rape: Granite baron Veeramani’s premises raided

What is the Veeramani case?

Case takes political turn

Summons issued to officials

NEW DELHI: The Central Crime Branch (CCB) has arrested Ganesan, a longtime aide of granite businessman and Gem Granites chief Veeramani, in connection with a POCSO case involving the alleged sexual abuse of minor girls.Ganesan is the fourth accused arrested in the case. Police said he had worked with Veeramani’s Gem Granites for 23 years and is currently employed with Balaji Global Enterprises.According to investigators, Ganesan had video clips on his mobile phone that purportedly showed Veeramani in an obscene act involving a minor girl. Police said he did not inform the authorities about the videos.The CCB is now investigating how Ganesan came to possess the clips and why he allegedly kept them without alerting police. Investigators are also examining his mobile phone to determine whether any data was deleted.Veeramani was arrested on August 29 along with two alleged accomplices after the Anti-Vice Squad (AVS) registered a case over the alleged rape of minor girls. The three accused were subsequently remanded in Puzhal Central Prison.Police said the case came to light after a USB drive containing a video clip purportedly showing Veeramani sexually assaulting a juvenile girl was recovered.Investigators identified the survivor and established that she was a minor when the alleged offence took place in 2019.The video was also examined as part of the investigation into the allegations against Veeramani.The investigation has also expanded to suspected financial transactions allegedly made to influence the earlier probe, police said.Investigators are examining bank transactions and the possible involvement of intermediaries in the movement of funds.The ruling TVK on Wednesday demanded that DMK president MK Stalin explain how the POCSO case involving Veeramani was handled when the DMK was in power, alleging that the investigation was allowed to weaken and questioning why a final report was filed.The TVK alleged that the case had been “buried”. The party also questioned former law minister S. Regupathy over his handling of video footage submitted in connection with the case.“Under whose pressure did the then Law Minister Regupathy allow the investigation to be weakened? What was the reason?” the TVK asked.The party also sought an explanation for the filing of the final report, alleging that it was submitted without a proper investigation.Chennai Central Crime Branch police have issued summons to Assistant Commissioner Yasmin and Anti-Vice Squad inspectors Mahesh Kumar and Rajalakshmi in connection with the sexual assault case against industrialist Veeramani.The three officials, who had earlier investigated and closed the case, have been asked to appear in person for an inquiry and provide their explanations, Chennai Police said.
Article Summary: Ganesan is the fourth accused arrested in the case. Ganesan had video clips on his mobile phone that purportedly showed veeramani in an obscene act involving a minor girl. Police said he did not inform the authorities about the videos. The investigation has also expanded to suspected financial transactions allegedly made to influence the earlier probe.
